screen1-a1.where: The top left corner: a blue rounded square with a white speech bubble in it.
screen1-a1.expectation: It takes me to my messages, this page.
screen1-a1.cue: The speech bubble, and the heading 'Messages' printed right beside it. It is lit up blue, as though it is the one I am on.

first_pass.why: There is no word on the button itself. I only connect it with messages because the heading happens to be next to it; on another page I would not know what it is.
first_pass.solution: The word 'Messages' underneath the picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the speech-bubble square at the top left takes you where you expected
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the first 'ATs' square in the left column. On that screen, press the speech-bubble square at the very top of the left column and see where you land. (one try covering the same box on screen2-a1, screen14-a1, screen26-a1, screen27-a1, screen28-a1, screen29-a1, screen30-a1, screen31-a1, screen32-a1, screen33-a1, screen34-a1, screen35-a1)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: where you land is not what you expected, or you could not tell until you arrived
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: you land where you expected
test_cases.what_happened: From the Messages screen I pressed the first 'ATs' square, then on that group page the grey speech-bubble square at the top of the left column. After a moment the Messages page came back: heading 'Messages', and the speech-bubble square turned blue.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: It took me where I guessed, and the heading confirmed it. The square itself still carries no word, so I am relying on the picture and a guess.

screen1-a2.where: The small magnifying glass at the top, just left of the 'Add Friends' button.
screen1-a2.cue: The magnifying glass. That has meant 'search' for as long as I have used a computer.

first_pass.why: A familiar picture that I do not have to learn. I would want to know what I am searching, but I would press it and see.

screen1-a3.where: The long grey button at the top with a small person-and-plus picture and the words 'Add Friends'.
screen1-a3.expectation: It lets me add a friend.

first_pass.why: The words say plainly what it does.

screen1-a4.where: The blue square with a white plus sign at the top right, beside 'Add Friends'.
screen1-a4.expectation: It adds or starts something new. Possibly a new conversation, possibly another way to add a friend.
screen1-a4.cue: Only the plus sign. There is no word.

first_pass.why: A plus sign tells me 'new' or 'add' but not what. It sits right beside a button that already says 'Add Friends', so I cannot tell how it is different. I would leave it alone.
first_pass.solution: A word on it, such as 'New message', so I know what it creates.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the blue plus shows what it adds, and whether that differs from 'Add Friends'
test_cases.action: Start on the Messages screen (the one headed 'Messages', with the speech-bubble square at the top left). Press the blue square with the white plus at the top right (not the 'Add Friends' button). Look at what opens and read its heading. (one try covering the same box on screen2-a4, screen14-a4)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the plus was for, or it is the same thing 'Add Friends' does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens has a heading in plain words that tells you what the plus did, and it is a different thing from 'Add Friends'
test_cases.what_happened: From the Messages screen I pressed the blue square with the white plus at the top right. After a moment a page opened with the heading 'New Message', a box beginning 'To:' with 'Search your friends', and a blue 'Add Friends' button at the bottom. So it starts a new message; it is not the same thing as 'Add Friends'.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: Once pressed, the heading tells me plainly what I have done and it is harmless. But the plus itself still says nothing before I press it, and next time I would have to press it again to find out.

screen1-a5.where: The first grey square in the left-hand column, with the letters 'ATs'.
screen1-a5.expectation: I have no idea. Perhaps it opens some group or account called 'ATs'.
screen1-a5.cue: Only the letters 'ATs' on a grey square. There are three squares that all say exactly the same thing.

first_pass.why: 'ATs' is an abbreviation I do not know, and there are three of them identical to each other. I cannot tell which is which, nor what any of them is. I would not remember which one I pressed last time.
first_pass.solution: Each square should carry its full name in ordinary words, and no two should look the same. A heading over the column saying what the list is would help.

screen2-a9.expectation: It lets me add a friend.

screen2-a10.where: The long bar at the bottom with the words 'Accessibility Testing', a little downward arrow, and 'Online' in small grey letters beneath.
screen2-a10.expectation: I think it concerns my own account. Pressing it might show my details, or let me change the word 'Online' to something else.

first_pass.why: It is my name, so I can guess it is about me, but nothing says whether pressing it changes my status, opens my page, or switches to another account. I would be pressing it to find out.
first_pass.solution: A plain word on it, such as 'My account' or 'Change whether I appear online', so I know before I press.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing your name bar shows what it is for

screen2-a10.closing_comment: It opened details about me, which was one of my guesses, but the small arrow promised a list and there was none. I can see it is my page, but I had to work that out from the contents.

screen6-a3.expectation: It makes a group already set up for playing games.

screen6-a4.expectation: It makes a group already set up for a school club.

first_pass.why: Plain words.

screen7-a1.where: The white X on a black square at the very top left.

screen7-a2.expectation: It might let me change my picture, or show it larger.

first_pass.why: There is no word, and I cannot tell whether pressing it changes my picture or merely looks at it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing your big round picture does what you expected
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. On your page, press your big round picture near the top. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a2, screen19-a2, screen20-a2)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected from a picture
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: On my own page I pressed the big round picture near the top. It did not change the picture or show it larger. A panel slid up headed 'Change Online Status', with choices 'Online', 'Idle', 'Do Not Disturb', 'Invisible' and 'Set a custom status'. I closed it with the back button without changing anything.

screen7-a2.closing_comment: The panel's heading is clear, but nothing about a picture of a face would ever tell me that pressing it changes whether I appear online. I would not have predicted it, and I would not remember it.

screen7-a3.where: The white speech bubble to the right of the picture, with a small plus sign and the words 'What have you been reading?' in slanted letters.
screen7-a3.expectation: I suppose I can write a short line about myself for others to see.
screen7-a3.cue: The plus sign and the question 'What have you been reading?'.

first_pass.why: It is a question, not an instruction. It does not say that what I write will be shown to other people, nor where.
first_pass.solution: A fixed label, such as 'Add a short status for others to see', that stays the same each time.

test_cases.targets: whether the speech bubble's purpose becomes plain once you press it
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press the speech bubble with the italic question beside your picture. test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the screen that opens still does not tell you what it is for or who would see it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen that opens tells you in plain words what it is for
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the speech bubble beside my picture. A screen opened headed 'Set your status', with a small copy of my card showing the bubble, a box labelled 'Status' containing 'What's your hot take?', a line 'Clear at  Tomorrow at 6:27 PM', and 'Save' at the top right. The keyboard came up. I left with the X without saving.

screen7-a3.closing_comment: Now I know it is a 'status' and that it clears itself tomorrow; the label 'Status' stays above the box, which is good. It still does not say in words who will see it, and 'hot take' is a phrase I do not know.

screen7-a4.where: The large name 'Accessibility Testing' with a small downward arrow, below the picture.
screen7-a4.expectation: It might show a list, perhaps to switch to another account.
screen7-a4.cue: The name and the small arrow.

first_pass.why: The arrow says something drops down, but nothing tells me what. I would press it to find out, and I may not remember afterwards what I found.
first_pass.solution: A word next to the arrow saying what the list is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing your name with the small arrow opens what you expected
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press your name with the small down arrow under your picture. Look at what opens. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a4, screen19-a4, screen20-a4)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected from your name and the arrow
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: On my page I pressed my name with the small down arrow. The same 'Change Online Status' panel came up that the big picture had opened. I closed it.

screen7-a4.closing_comment: I had guessed it might switch to another account. It does drop a list, with a clear heading, but not the one I expected, and the name and the picture turn out to do the same thing, which I would not have guessed.

screen7-a5.where: The wide blue button with a pencil: 'Edit Profile'.
screen7-a5.expectation: It lets me change the details on my page.
screen7-a5.cue: The words 'Edit Profile' and the pencil.

first_pass.why: Ordinary words.

screen7-a6.where: The word 'Main' in blue, under 'Edit Profile', on the left; it has a blue line under it.
screen7-a6.expectation: It shows the main part of my page, which is what I am looking at now.
screen7-a6.cue: The word 'Main', in blue, with a line beneath.

first_pass.why: 'Main' of what? I gather from the colour that it is the one chosen, but the word itself tells me little.
first_pass.solution: A plainer word, such as 'About me'.

screen7-a6.closing_comment: Comparing the two makes it a little plainer: 'Main' is just my ordinary page and 'Wishlist' is a separate list. The word 'Main' itself still names nothing.

screen7-a7.closing_comment: This matches my guess: things from the shop I would like. It is explained in a sentence, though 'heart the items' is an odd verb and it still does not say who else can see the list.

first_pass.why: A familiar close sign.

first_pass.solution: Say in plain words what it is, for example 'Pay for extra features', and the price.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen still tells you what you are searching through while you type

first_pass.why: A familiar back arrow.

screen11-a2.where: The first of the six small squares across the top: an arrow rising out of a tray, labelled 'Share Invite'.
screen11-a2.expectation: It sends an invitation to someone by way of some other programme on the telephone.

first_pass.why: The words tell me I am sending an invitation. I would find out how when I press it.

screen11-a3.where: The second small square: a chain link, labelled 'Copy Link'.
screen11-a3.expectation: It copies an invitation address so I can paste it somewhere else.
screen11-a3.cue: The words 'Copy Link' and the chain picture.

first_pass.why: I understand the words, but I would then have to remember that I had copied something invisible and carry it to another place. That is precisely the sort of thing I lose if my attention slips.
first_pass.solution: Show on screen what has been copied, and say plainly what to do with it next.

test_cases.targets: whether the app tells you what happened after 'Copy Link' and what to do next
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press 'Add Friends' at the top. Press 'Copy Link' and watch the screen. (one try covering the same box on screen13-a3, screen23-a3, screen25-a3)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you that something was copied or what to do with it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you plainly that the link was copied
test_cases.what_happened: On 'Add Friends' I pressed 'Copy Link'. The page itself did not change. A small grey card appeared at the bottom left showing 'https://discord.gg/9UFdjZHS' with a small x and two round picture-buttons. There was no word 'copied' and nothing about what to do next. A few seconds later the card was gone.

screen11-a3.closing_comment: I can just about see an address flash up, but nothing tells me in words that it was copied or what to do with it, and it vanishes before I could read it properly.

first_pass.solution: A plain description, such as 'Show a code your friend can scan with their phone'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing 'QR Code' settles whether you show a code or scan one
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press 'Add Friends' at the top. Press 'QR Code' and look at what opens, then go back. (one try covering the same box on screen13-a4, screen23-a4, screen25-a4)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you still cannot tell whether you are showing or scanning
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: it is plain whether you are showing or scanning
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'QR Code'. A panel came up headed 'Add Friend by QR Code' with a large black-and-white square pattern and the words 'Scan the QR Code to add testingaccessibility35_22402 as a friend'. I went back.

screen11-a4.closing_comment: Because it names me as the one to be added, I can work out that I show it and the other person scans it. 'Scan' at first reads as an instruction to me, so it took a moment.

first_pass.solution: 'Send by text message'.

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you land somewhere you did not expect, or cannot tell which 'Messages' it was
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: you land where you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'Messages' in the row of squares. It left this app entirely and opened the telephone's own text-message programme at 'New conversation', 'To: Type names, phone numbers, or emails', with the keyboard up. When I pressed back, that programme showed a 'Welcome! Customize how you're seen' page with a 'Continue as...' button; I did not press it, and reopened this app instead, which brought me back to 'Add Friends'. I sent nothing.

screen11-a5.closing_comment: It was my first guess, an ordinary text message, and the programme looks plainly different. But nothing warned me I was leaving the app, and getting back led me into another programme's welcome page.

screen11-a7.closing_comment: It went where I expected and it is plainly different from 'Messages'. Still, nothing said I was leaving the app, and a single wrong press on any of those 'Send' buttons would send an invitation to someone.

first_pass.why: The words say what it does. Whether I know my friend's user name is another matter, but I understand the button.

first_pass.why: Ordinary words.

first_pass.solution: Say it in plain words: 'Look through the names in your phone to find people you know here. We will ask first.'

test_cases.targets: whether the page after 'Find friends' explains in plain words what happens to your address book
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press 'Add Friends' at the top. Press 'Find friends' and read the page that opens. Do not press 'Allow'. Close it with the X. (one try covering the same box on screen13-a10, screen23-a10, screen25-a10)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the page does not tell you in plain words what will happen to your address book
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the page tells you in plain words what will happen before you agree
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'Find friends'. A page came up with an X at the top left, a box 'Find your friends — Sync your contacts to find people you know on Discord.' with a blue 'Allow' button, and at the bottom a switch already turned on: 'Allow contacts to add me — This allows people to send you friend requests if they have your phone number saved in their contacts.' I did not press 'Allow'; I closed it with the X.

screen11-a10.closing_comment: It uses the same word 'sync' and never says in plain words what would happen to my address book. And a switch was already turned on for me without my asking.

screen35-a14.closing_comment: My fear was that one press would put me on the air with strangers. It does not: it shows me the room first, says in plain words that it is for talking, and waits for me to press 'Join Voice'.

screen35-a15.where: The long bar at the bottom with the words 'Accessibility Testing', a little downward arrow, and 'Online' in small grey letters beneath.
screen35-a15.expectation: I think it concerns my own account. Pressing it might show my details, or let me change the word 'Online' to something else.
screen35-a15.cue: The name, the small arrow, and the word 'Online'. The arrow suggests a list will drop down, but not what is in it.

first_pass.why: It is my name, so I can guess it is about me, but nothing says whether pressing it changes my status, opens my page, or switches to another account. I would be pressing it to find out.
first_pass.solution: A plain word on it, such as 'My account' or 'Change whether I appear online', so I know before I press.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing your name bar shows what it is for
test_cases.action: Start on the Messages screen (the one headed 'Messages', with the speech-bubble square at the top left). Press your name 'Accessibility Testing' in the bar at the bottom (the words, not the round picture). Look at what opens. (one try covering the same box on screen1-a10, screen2-a10, screen14-a10, screen26-a15, screen27-a15, screen28-a15, screen29-a15, screen30-a15, screen31-a15, screen32-a15, screen33-a15, screen34-a15)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what the name and its small arrow led you to expect, or you still cannot tell what it is for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected from your name and its arrow
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed my name 'Accessibility Testing' in the bar at the bottom. No list dropped down, despite the little arrow. Instead my own page opened: the big picture, my name, 'Edit Profile', 'Main' and 'Wishlist', 'Orbs Balance', 'Friends', and the bar with Quests, Shop, Nitro and Settings. A pop-up card was also sitting on top of it saying 'Style your display name... Only with Nitro'. The page has no heading such as 'My page'.

screen35-a15.closing_comment: It opened details about me, which was one of my guesses, but the small arrow promised a list and there was none. I can see it is my page, but I had to work that out from the contents.

screen35-a16.where: A small box over the round blue picture at the bottom left, the cartoon face with a green dot beside it.
screen35-a16.expectation: I suppose it is my own picture, and pressing it would open my own page.
screen35-a16.cue: It sits beside my name at the bottom. The green dot might mean I am present.

first_pass.why: It is a cartoon face, not my photograph, and there is no word on it. I only connect it to me because my name is next to it.
first_pass.solution: The word 'My profile' under the picture, or my own photograph.

test_cases.targets: whether the round picture does what you expected, and whether it differs from pressing the name next to it
test_cases.action: Start on the Messages screen (the one headed 'Messages', with the speech-bubble square at the top left). Press the round picture at the bottom left and look at what opens. Go back, press the name next to it, and compare. (one try covering the same box on screen1-a11, screen2-a11, screen14-a11, screen26-a16, screen27-a16, screen28-a16, screen29-a16, screen30-a16, screen31-a16, screen32-a16, screen33-a16, screen34-a16)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the picture does something you did not expect, or you cannot tell whether it differs from the name
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the picture opens what you expected and you can tell how it relates to the name
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the round cartoon picture at the bottom left. It opened the very same page as my name did. The question in the speech bubble had changed again, now 'What's your hot take?'. I went back and pressed the name: the same page.

screen35-a16.closing_comment: The picture opens my page, as I guessed, and it does exactly the same as the name next to it, so the two are one thing. There is still no word on the picture; I am relying on the name beside it.

screen35-a17.where: The small bell in the bottom right corner of the bar at the foot of the screen.
screen35-a17.expectation: It would show me my alerts, the things the telephone calls notifications.
screen35-a17.cue: The picture of a bell. My own telephone uses a bell for the same thing.

first_pass.why: A bell for alerts is something I have known for years; I do not have to learn it.
